subject: ventures/chant-forge
professional: a Gregorian schola director who also engraves chant (checks pitches, modes and Latin diction against the Vatican Graduale / Liber Usualis and the score against MusicXML conventions), paired with a mastering engineer (checks LUFS, LRA and true peak against BS.1770 / EBU Tech 3342 and Spotify's delivery note). First checks: does the melody match the printed book note for note, is the Latin pronounced by the Liber Usualis rules, does the score open cleanly with sensible clefs, and does the loudness meter agree with a reference meter.

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write. (1) node cli.mjs corpus/dies-irae.gabc -o di.mid, read back with my own raw-byte Python SMF reader: first 19 pitches 53,52,53,50,52,48,50,50 | 53,53,55,53,52,50,48,52,53,52,50 = F E F D E C D D | F FG FE DC E F E D, the Liber Usualis / 1908 Graduale Dies irae ('Dies irae dies illa, Solvet saeclum in favilla'); 613 notes; tempo meta 483871 us = 124 BPM. (2) node cli.mjs corpus/veni-creator.gabc: 55,57,55,53,55,57,55,60,62,60 = sol la sol-fa sol la-sol do re do, the mode-8 Veni Creator incipit, final G3, mode 8 check passes. (3) ffmpeg-generated (not author) pink/brown noise + 220 Hz sine, 32 s, loud/quiet sections to exercise gating: master-cli -28.1 LUFS, LRA 7.8 LU, -15.93 dBTP; ffmpeg ebur128 -28.1 LUFS, LRA 8.1 LU, -16.0 dBFS peak (LRA within Tech 3342's +/-1 LU). Also ep-cli's 284 s Dies irae track: master-cli -14.0 LUFS / -2.75 dBTP, ffmpeg -14.0 / -2.8. (4) MusicXML from Dies irae and from Te Deum with --split-voices --baritones --second-tenors --choir octave --genre metal --sections both validate against the W3C MusicXML 4.0 XSD (xmllint --schema, fetched from w3c/musicxml v4.0); parts carry treble-8vb and bass clefs. (5) --organum on Dies irae: intervals {fourth 260, major third 108, second 96, unison 149}, 0 tritones, organal voice holds the C boundary under a D final as Musica enchiriadis prescribes. No number I recomputed was wrong; the Latin diction departures are scored under domain.
evidence.completeness: Ran each headline 'works now' item I could reach: GABC->MIDI (two pieces), --organum, --musicxml (plain and four-part split with sections), --split-voices/--baritones/--second-tenors/--choir, --genre metal --sections, master-cli on a foreign signal and on a built track, ep-cli examples/first-ep.json (built in under a minute: REPORT.md, cover.png, release.json, sources, tracks; 7 owner steps listed, no build faults). Served page https://marisstella.app/chant-forge/ returns 200; served-copy.mjs finds no placeholder origins. Browser studio features are covered by ep-page/ep-queue tests that passed in the suite (headless). Not run by me: scan.mjs against page scans (needs archive.org downloads). Everything I ran worked; the README is explicit that no person has listened and no release exists.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in ventures/chant-forge: 331 tests, 331 pass, 0 fail, 48.5 s. Five seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, all caught: BS.1770 relative gate -10 -> -20 LU (master.mjs:107; the previous audit's surviving mutant, now caught), organum boundary loosened by 2 semitones (organum.mjs:36), punctum mora pulses 1 -> 0 (gabc.mjs:17), accidentals no longer reset at word start (gabc.mjs:94), Spotify true-peak headroom 1 -> 2 dB (master.mjs:210). EBU Tech 3341/3342 tests are now in the suite. Not 4: the Latin diction rules have tests that encode the author's own (syllable-local) reading, so the gratia/mihi departures below pass them.
evidence.craft: Read gabc.mjs, organum.mjs, master.mjs (integratedLufs, platformPlayback), sing.mjs (latinVowel/latinOnset/latinCoda), cli.mjs usage. Zero dependencies, ES modules, small pure functions with comments that state rules and limits, deterministic output, browser-safe. Defects: gabc.mjs:192 still skips unknown characters silently (no warning); sing.mjs carries several rules that 'failed their registration' as opt-in code paths (README 1147-1449), accumulating untested-in-default branches; scan.mjs is 1,155 lines; the README is 2,961 lines of dated lab notebook, which makes the current state hard to find (counts against claims too).
evidence.claims: Checked: llms.txt now matches the code (previous medium defect fixed) except 'Run on 64 real GregoBase files' (llms.txt:31, README.md:2914) while the corpus holds 8 + 60 files plus six more gregobase-1908-* sets; README.md:16-17 pipeline overview still says stage 3 'Arrange: genre templates ... Not built' while genre.mjs, --genre and --sections ship and the page sells them; README.md:153 still says chant-forge.test.mjs has 8 tests (14 now); README.md:2959 is a 2026-11-03 status paragraph whose 'Next' list includes items since done (Te Deum from a pre-1929 book). Backed: 331 tests, EBU Tech 3341/3342 reports, MusicXML XSD validity (reproduced), ffmpeg agreement (reproduced), Spotify -14 LUFS / -1 and -2 dBTP rules (with others marked 'commonly reported'), 'nobody has listened' (honest and repeated). index.html has a rights note and MIT/support line but still no usage counter, against the repo's new-surface rule. Contradictions at the top of the README and a stale public summary keep this at 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked a producer's job: Dies irae -> men's-range MIDI with Latin lyric events, a four-part MusicXML score that validates and uses correct choral clefs, a metal backing with song sections, and a -14 LUFS release folder from ep-cli in under a minute. A producer gets a usable DAW starting point. Where they stall in the first hour: the chant is on an equal eighth-note pulse padded to bars (no Solesmes rhythm beyond mora/episema), the preview choir is synthetic and nobody has listened to anything, the built track has LRA 0.3 LU (a flat preview, not a mix), and no singer has tried the cue sheets or range splits. The intended result, an EP people stream, does not yet exist.
evidence.domain: Against the 1908 Graduale/Liber Usualis, Musica enchiriadis, MusicXML 4.0 and BS.1770/EBU R128: pitch reading, clefs, flat clef, accidental scope, modal finals, scan-checked corpus (Te Deum now from the 1908 Graduale, Salve Regina read against 1912/1913 books), organum boundary and occursus, MusicXML engraving and loudness all match practice. Departures a schola director would flag: Latin diction is syllable-local in sing.mjs:80-99, so 'ti' before a vowel is sung /ti/ not /tsi/ (gra-ti-a in Veni Creator verse 1; the Liber Usualis rule gives gratsia), the h of mihi/nihil is silent instead of /k/ (Dies irae 'Mihi quoque'), z is /z/ not /dz/, and xc before e/i is not /kʃ/; organum's 'third below' fallback only tries a major third and then a fifth (organum.mjs:35), an extension of the treatise, not its rule; fixed-pulse rhythm by design (disclosed).

defects.what: Latin diction is decided per syllable with no word context, so the sung preview departs from the Liber Usualis rules: 'ti' before a vowel is /ti/ not /tsi/ (gra-ti-a, Veni Creator verse 1), the h of mihi/nihil is silent instead of /k/ (Dies irae 'Mihi quoque'), z is /z/ not /dz/, xc before e/i is not /kʃ/. The tests encode the same reading, so they pass.

README's pipeline overview, the first thing a reader sees, says stage 3 'Arrange: genre templates ... Not built' while genre.mjs, --genre and --sections ship and the page offers them; the README is 2,961 lines of dated notes and its closing status paragraph (line 2959) is from 2026-11-03 with a stale 'Next' list.
README still says chant-forge.test.mjs has 8 tests; it has 14 (suite: 331).
llms.txt and README say the converter has run on 64 real GregoBase files; the corpus now holds 8 + 60 files plus six further gregobase-1908-* sets.
Unknown GABC characters are still skipped with no warning, so a misread neume gives a quiet wrong output.

Organum fallback when the fourth below is not in the chant's collection tries a major third then a fifth, never a minor third; the fifth is an extension of the Musica enchiriadis rule, not stated as such.

verdict: Chant Forge has grown from a converter slice into a broad, honest toolchain and its outputs are right: Dies irae and Veni Creator pitches match the printed melodies, loudness, LRA and true peak agree with ffmpeg ebur128 on a signal the author did not make, MusicXML (including a four-part split with sections) validates against the W3C 4.0 XSD, and the organum obeys the Musica enchiriadis boundary with no tritones. 331 of 331 tests pass and all five seeded mutations were caught, including the loudness gate that survived last time. Of the six 2026-11-08 defects, three are closed (gate test, llms.txt, pre-1929 sources) and three low ones remain. It does not meet the bar on claims: the README's own pipeline summary still says arrangement is not built, test and file counts are stale, and the page lacks the usage counter. A schola director would also flag the sung Latin (gratia as 'ti', mihi with a silent h), and nobody has listened to any output. Cheapest fixes: correct README.md:16-17 and :153, the '64 files' line in llms.txt:31, and add word-context rules for ti+vowel and mihi/nihil in sing.mjs.
